newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Korona starts NFI fund on June 10.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Korona starts NFI fund on June 10.

text.p: Mutual fund company TFP Korona SA will start on June 10 to sell units of a new fund, investing in National Investment Funds' (NFI) shares and NFI units of Poland's mass privatisation scheme, Korona officials said.
Korona president David Glasgow told a news conference on Monday that the company's fourth fund would promise investors higher returns but at a higher risk than other funds.
"The (mass privatisation) fund will offer the highest potential returns (from among all our funds) but at the highest level of risk," Glasgow said.
Korona's chief strategist Geoffrey Skipper said the new fund should benefit from a high growth rate in the manufacturing sector, likely to exceed overall economic growth.
"Industrial output is predicted to grow by 8-10 percent this year, above the overall GDP growth, " Skipper said.
He said sales growth of companies in National Investment Funds' portfolios might be slower than the overall industrial growth but should still top the projected economic growth rate.
The government forecasts 1997 GDP growth at 5.5 percent and analysts' predictions vary between five and six percent.
Under Poland's mass privatisation scheme, shares in about 500 mid-sized companies are allocated in 15 NFIs, which are scheduled to start bourse trade on June 12.
About 26 million Poles have bought a participation unit in the scheme. These are currently traded on the bourse and since May 12 they have been exchangeable for shares in the NFIs.
